clue.text: Help this punter put in order for game

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A punter is told to organise their help before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' is the anagram signal. The answer is a children's party game in which a shoe is passed secretly round a circle of players.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional parlour game played by children, passing a slipper around a ring of players.

clue.text: All give it for maximum effort

definitions.meaning: everything, the full amount, expressed as a proportion
what you are told to give when trying as hard as you possibly can

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the entire amount and also total commitment, as in giving everything you have.

clue.text: Token in name only

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, small and symbolic, like a token payment
existing as a title without real substance

explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum is a token one, and a nominal leader holds the title but no real power.

clue.text: I get point playing, going carefully

indicators.note: something playing is in action and moving about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone scores a point in a game while moving cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges I GET POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on the tips of the toes is a way of moving cautiously and quietly.

clue.text: Issued the final mandate, perhaps

indicators.note: the final letter of the word just before it is taken
perhaps suggests a possible other form of the word, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official order, the last one, was sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' takes E from 'the'; 'perhaps' rearranges MANDATE to MANATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means came out or was given off from a source, a synonym of issued.

clue.text: General method to get elbowroom

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A commanding officer adopts a technique to gain some space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is the crossword staple for Lee, commander of the southern army in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom or room to manoeuvre, the figurative space that elbowroom also names.

clue.text: Edible item without question causes irritation

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a pie is something you can eat

explanation.surface: A snack served with no questions asked annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense of outside, so the pastry dish goes round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of resentment or hurt pride, a form of annoyance.

clue.text: It's always estimated as extremely high

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for the noun, the very highest place

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
EST is the usual abbreviation for estimated

explanation.surface: A measurement is always reckoned to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the mountain is the byword for something extremely high.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak is the world's tallest mountain, the archetype of great height.

clue.text: Held down slates, we hear, being concealed

parts.note: kept under means held down or suppressed

indicators.note: signals that a word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, as is to rap

explanation.surface: Roofing tiles are held in place while hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slates' looks like roofing material but is the verb to criticise; RAPS and WRAPS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept under wraps is an idiom meaning kept secret or hidden.

clue.text: Specify coat that's to be put on the door

definitions.text: to be put on the door

parts.note: to name something is to specify it
to plate is to coat with a thin layer of metal

explanation.surface: Someone names the paint coat to be applied to a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaque bearing a person's name is typically fixed to their front or office entrance.

clue.text: Indication, they say, for American line

indicators.note: signals that a word is spoken aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a cue is a signal or indication to act

explanation.surface: A signal for an American railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The British word for a line of people waiting is defined by what Americans call it, a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of waiting people in American usage is called by this word in Britain.

clue.text: Partly erroneous copy

indicators.note: only part of the following word is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Something is partly mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' marks RONEO inside erRONEOus. A Roneo was a stencil duplicating machine; to roneo is to copy with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Roneo is a trade name for a stencil duplicator, so to roneo a document is to reproduce it.

clue.text: Getting a place below is a humiliation

parts.note: a basement is a storey below ground level

explanation.surface: Being given a seat lower down feels degrading.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is the state of being humbled or degraded, which is what humiliation means.

clue.text: Music provider lured mice mostly abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so these letters are rearranged
most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An instrument tempts rodents away overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the E of MICE; 'abroad' rearranges LURED and MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The dulcimer is a stringed instrument, so it is something that makes music.

clue.text: Playwright round the North in Lancashire

definitions.note: describes a place found in that county

parts.note: Robert Bolt wrote A Man for All Seasons
a round shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: A dramatist travels around the north of England's Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; Bolton is a large town there.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a description: this town lies in Lancashire, near Manchester.

clue.text: I'm certainly not bone idle

parts.note: spoken by a practitioner whose work is with bones, so they are always busy with bones

explanation.definitionFit: This therapist manipulates bones and joints, so is never idle where bones are concerned.

clue.text: Composition on sure thing in firm

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the firm's abbreviation

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a cert is a certainty, especially in betting

explanation.surface: A company bets on a dead certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the two pieces sit inside the abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical work for soloist and orchestra, a type of composition.

clue.text: Keep in — or, alternatively, eg cane?

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of letters is called for

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether to keep a pupil in or use the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternatively' rearranges EG CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To encage is to shut inside a cage, so to confine or keep in.

clue.text: Circle round terrace in French company

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the French abbreviation

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie
a round shape resembles the letter O
Ter. is the address abbreviation for terrace

explanation.surface: A ring of people goes round a terrace with a French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; Cie is how French firms abbreviate compagnie, as Co is used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, and a circle is a set of friends or associates.

clue.text: Observe at length the reference below

indicators.note: the word for observing goes at the end, placed after the length

parts.note: a foot is a unit of length
to note something is to observe it

explanation.surface: Someone notes the lengthy reference beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the observing word after the unit of length, as if at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a note printed at the bottom of a page, referred to from the text above.

clue.text: Bristol centre overlooked taking a turn going round city

indicators.note: a turn changes position, so these letters are rearranged
the middle letter of the word is skipped over

explanation.surface: Drivers miss the centre of Bristol by taking a road around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre overlooked' drops S from BRISTOL; 'turn' rearranges BRITOL with A.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road is a ring road that circles a city.

clue.text: Pollarded trees forming curved structures

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: larches are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Cut-back trees form bending shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pollarded' cuts the top letter L off LARCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Arches are curved structures spanning an opening.

clue.text: Without exception included in a class

definitions.meaning: relating to or placed in a category

explanation.definitionFit: Categoric means absolute and unqualified, and also belonging to a category.

clue.text: Plot involving good man missing line?

indicators.note: the following letter is absent from the name

parts.note: Ralph is a man's name

explanation.surface: A conspiracy involving a good man who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes L out of RALPH.
explanation.definitionFit: To graph data is to plot it on a chart.

clue.text: River bend makes a neat arc

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a bow is a curved shape, an arc

explanation.surface: A river curves in a tidy arc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy but is the archaic term for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is a U-shaped meander of a river.

clue.text: Not quite typical as a constellation

indicators.note: the word is not complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: normal means typical or usual

explanation.surface: A star pattern is described as not entirely ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final L from NORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma, the Carpenter's Square, is a small southern constellation.

clue.text: There a lab prepared an aromatic drink

indicators.note: something prepared is made up, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A laboratory makes a fragrant beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges THERE A LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs in hot water is a fragrant beverage.

clue.text: Not a very nice spirit

parts.note: an understated description of a demon from the Faust legend

explanation.definitionFit: This devil of German legend buys Faust's soul, a wicked spirit indeed.
